verdict.rationale: Cursor's core agent interaction model is natural-language driven: chat/agent prompts in the IDE, CLI (`agent -p "..."`), Slack, and cloud agents all accept plain-language instructions, and features like /automate explicitly let users 'describe the workflow you want in plain language' to configure automations. This is corroborated by extensive first-party docs across IDE, CLI, and cloud agent surfaces, though independent hands-on confirmation specifically of NL command fidelity is thin. Missing for 10: independent/third-party verification that natural-language commands reliably produce correct actions (community evidence only covers unrelated complaints), and no benchmark of NL command success/failure rates.
